title: Depth drops by one modulo a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), $M\neq0$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $x\in\mathfrak m$ a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $x$ on $M$ is injective). Then $M/xM\neq0$, $\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is a finite integer $\ge1$, and $\operatorname{depth}(M/xM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$, where $\operatorname{depth}=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}$ is the depth of a finite $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-depth].

proof.text: Nakayama, as Mathlib nontrivial_quotSMulTop_of_mem_maximalIdeal and top_ne_ideal_smul_of_le_jacobson_annihilator, gives a nonzero finite quotient Q=M/xM and mM != M, mQ != Q. The definitions therefore express both depths as suprema of lengths of regular lists in m.

proof.text: The support-dimension depth bound and Module.supportDim_le_ringKrullDim bound depth(M) by the finite Krull dimension of R. Thus depth(M)=d for a natural number d. The singleton [x] is regular, so 1 <= d. The finite supremum of natural-number lengths is attained: choose a regular list rs of length d in m.

proof.text: For any regular list on M of length n+1 in m, Rees condition (4) -> (1) gives Ext^i(N,M)=0 for all i<n+1 and all finite N supported in V(m). In the long exact Ext sequence of 0 -> M --x--> M -> Q -> 0, the exact window Ext^i(N,M) -> Ext^i(N,Q) -> Ext^(i+1)(N,M) has both outer terms zero when i<n. Therefore Ext^i(N,Q)=0. Rees condition (1) -> (4) gives a regular list of length n on Q in m. To accommodate independent universes, apply this argument to ULift M and transfer the input list and the resulting prepended list through ULift.moduleEquiv; isRegular_cons_iff transfers the tail back to Q.

proof.text: Apply the previous step to the attained regular list of length d, with n=d-1, to obtain depth(Q)>=d-1. Conversely every regular list qs on Q in m prepends with x to a regular list on M (Mathlib isRegular_cons_iff). Its length plus one is at most d, so its length is at most d-1. Taking the supremum gives depth(Q)<=d-1. Combine both inequalities.
